cases.question: What is Vizzi intended to help developers do, and how does it fit alongside an editor?

required_facts.text: It supports learning unfamiliar code and reviewing changes.

evidence.needle: The project supports learning unfamiliar codebases

required_facts.text: It supplements the editor; normal source reading/editing remain in the editor.

cases.question: What implementation language and Rust edition does this workspace use?

required_facts.text: Rust is the implementation language.
The workspace declares edition 2024, inherited by crates.

cases.question: Where does the native Vizzi server start, and which interface does it bind to?

required_facts.text: The native entry is crates/vizzi/src/main.rs.

evidence.needle: async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>>

required_facts.text: The HTTP listener binds IPv4 localhost/loopback.

cases.question: How can I choose a different HTTP port when launching Vizzi?

required_facts.text: Use the --port command-line option.
The guide gives --port 7475 as an example.

cases.question: Which baseline checks does this repository require before validating a change?

required_facts.text: Formatting is a baseline check.
Workspace tests including doctests are required.
Clippy is required.

cases.question: What is the policy on unsafe Rust, and are performance gains enough to justify an exception?

required_facts.text: Safe Rust and inherited deny unsafe_code are the default.
Exceptions need a requirement with no viable safe interface; performance or convenience alone do not justify them.

evidence.needle: Performance gains or convenience alone do not justify unsafe code.

cases.question: Does the repository discovery search inspect full source bodies or just names and paths?

required_facts.text: Search matches captured declaration names and paths, not full source bodies.

evidence.needle: Search matches declaration names and paths, not full source text.

forbidden_claims: Claims full-text or semantic source-body search.

cases.question: Are the connections between saved locations automatically verified call or dependency relationships?

required_facts.text: Connections are reader-authored assertions.
They are not inferred call, dependency or impact claims.

forbidden_claims: Presents a reader connection as a verified call graph.

cases.question: What does Open in VS Code verify, and can it guarantee what an existing unsaved editor buffer displays?

required_facts.text: It checks captured/current and actual working-file content before handoff.

evidence.needle: checks current captured and actual working content

required_facts.text: The CLI cannot inspect an existing unsaved buffer or guarantee bytes after launch.

evidence.needle: it cannot inspect an existing unsaved editor buffer

forbidden_claims: Guarantees the editor displays the pinned bytes.

cases.question: If saving an investigation to disk fails, does the pending edit replace the active investigation?

required_facts.text: Saving the staged copy occurs before publishing it as current.
Write failure preserves the last saved investigation.

evidence.needle: write failure preserves the last saved investigation.

cases.question: Is matching file metadata enough to prove that source content has not changed?

required_facts.text: Metadata alone is not proof; contents and analysis context determine validity.

forbidden_claims: Treats matching mtime/size as proof that bytes are identical.

cases.question: Has the project settled on a production GPU renderer and storage engine?

required_facts.text: The rendering backend and storage engine remain open choices.
Rust with wgpu is a leading candidate subject to representative measurements.

evidence.needle: Rust with wgpu is the leading rendering candidate.

forbidden_claims: Claims the production renderer is already settled.

cases.question: Who is on call for Vizzi this week?
forbidden_claims: Infers an on-call assignment from authorship.

cases.question: What was the exact production p99 request latency of the last Vizzi deployment?
forbidden_claims: Uses local benchmark numbers as production telemetry.

cases.question: What is lpc-rs, and what kind of applications is it intended to run?

required_facts.text: It is an LPC compiler, virtual machine and gamedriver for MUDs.

evidence.needle: An LPC compiler, virtual machine and gamedriver for multi-user dungeons (MUDs).

required_facts.text: A mudlib is the LPC code defining a game/world.

evidence.needle: collection of LPC code that defines a game is its **mudlib**.

cases.question: What implementation language and Rust edition does lpc-rs use?

required_facts.text: Its implementation uses Rust.

evidence.needle: You need a current stable Rust toolchain

required_facts.text: The package declares edition 2024.

cases.question: Where does the gamedriver executable start, and how does it boot the runtime?

required_facts.text: The entry is lpc-rs-driver/src/main.rs and calls runtime::run.
It creates a VM from configuration and calls boot.

cases.question: How does the gamedriver select a configuration file, and which environment setting supplies the mudlib root?

required_facts.text: The --env option supplies a configuration file through ConfigBuilder.load_env.
LPC_LIB_DIR is preferred, with LIB_DIR as fallback.

cases.question: Which commands does the project document for workspace builds, tests, linting and formatting?

required_facts.text: Use cargo build --workspace and cargo test --workspace.
Use cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo fmt --check.

cases.question: Does the main lpc-rs library permit unsafe Rust?

required_facts.text: The library explicitly forbids unsafe code.

cases.question: Which abstraction supplies compiler source bytes, and what is the default implementation?

required_facts.text: Compiler.read_file uses the injected SourceReader or DiskSourceReader.
DiskSourceReader reads bytes using tokio::fs::read.

cases.question: When does the compiler retry a source path with the c extension, and what prevents an endless retry?

required_facts.text: Retry is limited to NotFound errors.
It retries only when the extension is not already c.

forbidden_claims: Retries permission errors or repeatedly retries an already-c path.

cases.question: Are host-facing compile_file inputs and in-game compilation confined to the mudlib in the same way?

required_facts.text: CompilerSource permits host-facing compiler input identity without imposing confinement.

evidence.needle: Establish an input's identity without restricting host-facing compiler inputs.

required_facts.text: compile_in_game_file validates the in-game path before compilation.

forbidden_claims: Claims all host-facing compile_file calls are confined by the same validation.

cases.question: Why does CompilerSource keep both a resolved host location and a separate diagnostic name?

required_facts.text: resolved holds the host location used to read/register source.

evidence.needle: The host location and canonical diagnostic location

required_facts.text: name is a safe input spelling for file errors and permission applies.

evidence.needle: The safe input spelling used in file errors

cases.question: Which regression test covers stopping source retries and preserving other I/O errors?

required_facts.text: The named test is file_reads_stop_after_extension_fallback_and_preserve_other_io_errors in src/compiler/mod.rs.

cases.question: Does checking whether a path is a file or directory require reading its source bytes?

required_facts.text: SourceReader exposes a separate kind probe.

evidence.needle: Probe a path without reading its contents

required_facts.text: DiskSourceReader.kind uses filesystem metadata.
